audit.whatIsWrong: The packet itself raises the defect: Illaoi wins 56.29% over 286 games, yet the page is rated 8.5/10 'Hard matchup' and the chart hands Quinn five of seven stages.
audit.why: One of the two is wrong and the data cannot settle which — 286 games is a thin sample, and a lane can be statistically won while feeling losing. I aligned the chart to the packet (the only authority the brief gives me) and left the difficulty tokens for the user.
audit.corrected: Chart aligned to packet; diff FAV / 8.5 left in place. See questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 4 and 5 read Skill, Quinn, Skill; the packet says Quinn, Illaoi, Illaoi.
audit.why: whys[3] says the ranged blind-and-kite pattern keeps level 4-5 firmly hers, and whys[4]/whys[5] both say the R window and first item favour you. The tokens contradicted their own text. The whys were also mislabelled by level ('At 5' on the Level 6 row, 'At 6' on the First item row).
audit.corrected: phases[3]/win[3] to Quinn, phases[4]/win[4] and phases[5]/win[5] to Illaoi as matched pairs, with whys[4] and whys[5] relabelled to the levels their rows actually represent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vault was described only as a disengage, and Blinding Assault was credited with killing tentacle procs.
audit.why: Riot's text for Vault: she dashes to the target, slows it, briefly interrupts it, and lands near her maximum attack range away — so it is an interrupt on you as well as her escape, on 12/11/10/9/8s. Blinding Assault marks the target and hinders its vision; whether that blind also suppresses tentacle swings is not in the file, so I removed the claim rather than assert it.
audit.corrected: Vault written as dash + interrupt + reposition with its 12s rank-1 cooldown; the blind stated only as turning off your autos.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Vault' appeared everywhere with no number.
audit.why: Vault at 12s rank 1 is the entire engage window in a lane where you otherwise cannot touch her.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing recorded about whether Blinding Assault's blind affects tentacle swings, or whether Vault's interrupt can cancel Illaoi's casts.
audit.why: Neither is in Riot's text. Both would change how the level-6 all-in is played, so they are worth a verified answer rather than a guess.
sources: brief enemyKit Q and E descriptions

edits.before: At 5 your R gap-close finally gives you a landed-E kill window, favouring you.
edits.after: At 6 your R gap-close finally gives you a landed-E kill window, favouring you.

edits.before: At 6 R plus stacked tentacles let one E burst her squishy frame in your favour.
edits.after: With first item, R plus stacked tentacles let one landed E burst her squishy frame.

edits.before: This is Quinn's dominant window: she kites you with Q Blinding Assault (blinds your autos, killing your Q tentacle procs) and E Vault to disengage every time you approach. You have almost no way to land E Test of Spirit on a ranged champ who dashes away — just farm under tower and concede the poke.
edits.after: This is Quinn's dominant window: Blinding Assault (Q) turns off your autos, and Vault (E) dashes in, briefly interrupts you, then throws her back to attack range — 12s at rank 1. Test of Spirit rarely lands on a champion who leaves the moment you step up, so farm under tower and concede the poke.

edits.before: At 6 you finally have counterplay: R Leap of Faith closes the gap and drops the tentacle ring, and if you catch her Vault on cooldown you can E her soul and burst her squishy frame. Flash-E or fight in tight spaces where she can't kite.
edits.after: At 6 you finally have counterplay: Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle for every champion it hits, so it opens the fight rather than ending it. Catch Vault on its 12s and one Test of Spirit ends a squishy with no sustain — Flash-E, or fight in tight ground.

edits.before: Blind your autos with Q to negate tentacle procs
edits.after: Blind your autos with Blinding Assault (Q)

notes: The packet flags its own contradiction here and it is real: 56.29% for Illaoi against an 8.5/10 'Hard matchup' rating and a chart that gives Quinn five stages. I aligned the chart to the packet and did not touch diff/diffRating — that call needs the user. Also fixed a level-label drift: whys[4] said 'At 5' on the Level 6 row and whys[5] said 'At 6' on the First item row. Dropped the unverified claim that her blind kills tentacle procs; Riot's text does not say it.
